topIssues.title: test(cloud): add a fail-closed, self-cleaning dedicated-agent chat lane
topIssues.author: NubsCarson
topIssues.body:
## Problem

Eliza currently has no canonical live lane that proves a **managed dedicated** Cloud agent can be provisioned on staging, answer a real proof-token chat turn through both bridge and SSE paths, and be cleaned up without silently exercising the shared tier.

This is a correctness/coverage bug, not a latency optimization. Several existing lanes appear to cover this path but do not:

- `hetzner-e2e.yml` is the only current workflow that combines a real proof-token `message.send` turn with raw-server teardown. It is blocked by the rejected isolated `HCLOUD_TOKEN_CI` (HTTP 401; #15616). The broader `HCLOUD_APPS_TOKEN` must not replace that scoped credential.
- `cloud-provisioning-e2e.mjs` and `live-cloud-provision-smoke.ts` create agents without `alwaysOn`/an equivalent dedicated-tier request. Current tier selection therefore defaults them to `shared`, even though their comments call the result Hetzner-backed.
- `cloud-provisioning-e2e.mjs` proves only `/api/status|health|me`; it does not send a real chat turn or delete the fresh agent.
- `live-cloud-provision-smoke.ts` has proof-token bridge/SSE checks and cleanup, but no workflow invokes it. With the current shared default, its pairing-token assertion is incompatible with the created tier. SIWE cleanup also leaves its disposable organization behind.
- `app-live-e2e.yml` wires `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY`, while the repository has `ELIZACLOUD_API_KEY`. Recent cloud-login/provision/chat jobs report green with the sole Playwright test skipped because the key is empty (for example job `86628737358`). This is green-by-skip, not live evidence.
- `launch-hardening-8756.yml` and the mobile Cloud provisioning job are status-only and do not prove dedicated chat or full cleanup. Recent mobile success reused a shared agent and completed in about 1.3 seconds.

The staging Cloud bearer itself is healthy: the latest Hetzner E2E reached and passed the Cloud auth preflight before the independent Hetzner-token 401. Staging `/api/health` also serves the expected current commit. The missing piece is truthful harness wiring.

## Why this matters

Without a fail-closed dedicated lane, shared-runtime success and skipped tests can be mistaken for proof of the Worker → dedicated router → Headscale → agent path. That leaves the final acceptance in #15347 and the dedicated leg of #16079 unverified.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add one manual/scheduled staging workflow that uses the existing managed staging provisioner and the existing repository Cloud credential; do not require or substitute the broader apps-project Hetzner token.
- Create a unique canary explicitly as dedicated (`alwaysOn: true` or the current canonical equivalent) and require the returned tier/state to be dedicated, running, database-ready, heartbeat-fresh, and mesh-addressed.
- Fail closed if the credential is missing, a test skips, the response is a canned/fabricated fallback, or the actual tier/path differs from the declared dedicated path.
- Send nonce-bearing real turns through both central bridge and dedicated SSE. Require clean completion and proof match.
- Capture privacy-safe timings/trace/path fields only; never emit credentials, prompts, model output, raw provider bodies, agent IDs, or hostnames.
- In `finally`, delete only the unique agent created by the run and clean up the disposable user/organization. Cleanup failure must fail the lane or leave an explicit reaper artifact.
- Add a no-unbounded-autoscale/cost guard or an explicitly bounded canary-capacity contract.
- Fix the App Live secret-name drift and make a zero-executed-test/skip outcome red for the declared Cloud chat job.
- Correct stale “Hetzner-backed” comments/tests so shared and dedicated coverage cannot be confused.
- Link a successful exact-deploy-SHA run back to #15347 and #16079.

## Evidence

- Latest fail-closed raw Hetzner run: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29184646484
- Prior manual credential recheck: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29164481453
- Related credential blocker: #15616
- Dedicated ingress acceptance tracker: #15347
- End-to-end telemetry tracker: #16079

topIssues.title: perf(core): composeState serializes embedding-gated providers — 0.7-3.4s floor before Stage-1 on every turn
topIssues.author: NubsCarson
topIssues.body:
## Problem

`composeState` serializes embedding-gated providers ahead of every Stage-1 call. On a direct-Cerebras deployment (fast models, telemetry below), the context-assembly floor is **0.7–3.4s per turn before the routing model even starts**:

```
 total  ttreply  stage1  embed  compose  relconv  chatctx
  3351     3156    1176   1984     1600     1598      794
  6042     5853    1650   1012     2329     1963     1442
  7375     7212    1666   1447     2445     2131     1345
  4478     4232    1804   2559     1834     1833      538
  6322     6047    2010   1579     2248     1789     2243
```
(`InferenceTiming` spans; median composeState 1.2s across 20 live turns; the two ~15ms rows are reused-state turns, showing the ceiling when assembly is skipped.)

`model:TEXT_EMBEDDING` runs ×2 (query embedding for `relevant-conversations` + one more) and `PLATFORM_CHAT_CONTEXT` adds 0.3–3.4s. On a 1.2s-stage-1 backend this floor is 40–60% of time-to-reply.

## Ask

Make the embedding-gated providers non-blocking or degrading: kick off `relevant-conversations` (and its embeddings) in parallel with the fast providers and give it a soft deadline — when it misses, compose without it rather than serializing every turn behind it. `PLATFORM_CHAT_CONTEXT` deserves the same soft-deadline treatment.

Telemetry: captured on a live Discord agent, Cerebras direct (gemma-4-31b small / zai-glm-4.7 large), develop @ 3e47d12ba03.

topIssues.title: [staging][ops] Staging agents never join headscale — all 48 running agents have empty headscale_ip, so the CP nginx router 404s the worker→CP→agent hop (chat dead-ends after #15205)
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## The layer under #15205
With the CF wildcard + TLS fixed (#15205), the app's per-agent calls now correctly reach `https://<id>.staging.elizacloud.ai` on the STAGING worker (verified: valid `*.staging.elizacloud.ai` cert, request lands on the staging cloud-api worker, no longer the prod one). But the chat still dead-ends: every `/api/*` call returns **HTTP 404 from Cloudflare with no CORS header** → browser reports `No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin'`.

## Root cause (systemic, not per-agent)
The worker's `handleDedicatedAgentProxy` → `proxyToOrigin` forwards to `AGENT_ROUTER_ORIGIN_HOST = eliza-staging-1.elizacloud.ai` (the staging CP). The CP runs **nginx** (:80/:443) which routes `<id>.staging.elizacloud.ai` to the agent over the **headscale tailnet** via the agent's `headscale_ip`. But:
- **All 48 running staging agents have `headscale_ip` NULL/empty** (`SELECT (headscale_ip IS NULL OR headscale_ip='') , count(*) FROM agent_sandboxes WHERE status='running'` → `t | 48`).
- **`headscale nodes list` on the CP shows NO online agent-tagged node** — only `cp-staging-router` (tag:eliza-proxy, online) and two `robot-tstest`/`robot-tstest2` (tag:agent) **offline since 2026-06-16**.

So staging agent containers are provisioned + running + serving on their node bridge (`bridge_url` is set, e.g. `http://91.98.38.74:19006`), but they **never join the headscale mesh**, so the CP router has no tailnet address to reach them → 404. The agent's own CORS (`resolveCorsOrigin`, which allows any origin when `ELIZA_CLOUD_PROVISIONED=1`) is never reached because the request dies at the CP hop.

## Why it surfaced only now
Nobody ever got a staging agent reachable end-to-end before tonight (DB split #15160 → image boot #15196 → wildcard/TLS #15205 all had to land first). This is the next distinct gap in the same 'staging never fully mirrored prod' class, adjacent to the known prod-parity headscale gap.

## What to investigate
Why staging agent containers don't join headscale: is the tailscale-up / headscale pre-auth-key step injected at provision time (the staging worker HAS `HEADSCALE_PUBLIC_URL`/`HEADSCALE_API_URL`/`HEADSCALE_USER=tunnel`) actually running in the container, and is the provisioning worker recording `headscale_ip` back to `agent_sandboxes`? Either the join is failing/skipped or the IP is never persisted. Fixing it should light up all 48 agents at once.

## Scope
Systemic (48/48 agents), needs the headscale/tailnet provisioning path debugged — an infra workstream, not a config toggle. #15205's edge routing is done and verified; this is the CP→agent hop. [stan-cloud]

## What (admin action, exact)

As repo admin, enable branch protection (or equivalent rulesets) on **`develop` AND `main`** requiring these 9 status checks — all of which now exist and run green at develop tip:

9. `stale-base guard`

Plus (recommended): require a PR before merging, block force-pushes, and keep admins-can-bypass off for `main`.

```
gh api repos/elizaOS/eliza/branches/develop --jq .protected  → false

gh api repos/elizaOS/eliza/rules/branches/develop            → []
```

Both branches are fully unprotected: any push-access account (or agent) can merge a red PR or push directly, and every check above is advisory-only.

NubsCarson fleet permission on this repo is `push: true, admin: false` (verified via `gh api repos/elizaOS/eliza --jq .permissions`). Branch protection / rulesets are repo-admin-only API surfaces — the PUT returns 403 for us. Only @lalalune (org admin) can flip this.

- The entire #11853 lane investment (all 9 lanes made green) becomes *enforced* instead of advisory — this is the explicitly deferred "Enforcement flip (step 2)" from #11853's closeout.
- Blocks the #11271 class of incident (stale-base mass-revert reached develop; the `stale-base guard` check exists but is unenforced today).
- Blocks red merges to `main` ahead of prod deploys.

## Relationship to #12719 (merge queue)

#12719 is the richer end-state for `develop` (merge-queue ruleset + single aggregate check). If shaw prefers to land #12719 directly, that supersedes the `develop` half of this issue — but `main` protection is needed either way, and this issue is the 5-minute fallback that stops red merges **now** without waiting on the merge-queue workflow prerequisite.

topIssues.title: bug(plugin-openai): Cerebras zai-glm-4.7 returns empty text ~50% of the time on capped max_tokens calls (not classified as a reasoning model)
topIssues.author: NubsCarson
topIssues.body:
## Problem

`zai-glm-4.7` — the default `TEXT_LARGE` model on Cerebras since #16261 — is a hybrid reasoning model (streams a separate `reasoning` delta channel), but `isReasoningModel()` in `plugins/plugin-openai/models/text.ts` does not match it. Two consequences on a local Cerebras runtime (`ELIZA_PROVIDER=cerebras`, `OPENAI_LARGE_MODEL=zai-glm-4.7`):

1. The Cerebras-mode `reasoning_effort: "low"` default (added for exactly this failure on `gpt-oss-120b`) never applies to GLM, so its reasoning runs unbounded.
2. `providerOptions.eliza.thinking = "off"` — set by core's planner loop (`packages/core/src/runtime/planner-loop.ts:1549`), Stage-1 formatting calls (`packages/core/src/services/message.ts:8770`), and the app-model-tester — is silently ignored by plugin-openai, while plugin-elizacloud maps it to each Cerebras model's suppression value (`resolveCerebrasThinkingOffReasoningEffort`, `plugins/plugin-elizacloud/src/models/text.ts:366`).

With a capped `max_tokens` the model spends the entire budget on hidden reasoning and returns **empty visible content** with `finish_reason: "length"`.

## Reproduction (live Cerebras, wire-captured via a logging proxy)

`POST /api/model-tester/run {"test":"text-large"}` on a default local Cerebras setup, 8 runs. Every request went out as `{"model":"zai-glm-4.7","max_tokens":160}` with **no** `reasoning_effort`:

```
4x  finish_reason:"length"  reasoning_tokens:160/160  → "TEXT_LARGE returned empty text"
4x  finish_reason:"stop"    reasoning_tokens:62–157   → "pong"
```

~50% failure, purely dependent on how long GLM happens to reason. Direct curl confirms the mechanism: `reasoning_effort:"low"` bounds reasoning (~20–30 tokens), and `reasoning_effort:"none"` (accepted by gemma/GLM, rejected by gpt-oss) eliminates it entirely (`reasoning_tokens: 0`).

## Fix

PR incoming, mirroring plugin-elizacloud's settled semantics:

- add the GLM family to `isReasoningModel()` so the Cerebras `"low"` default applies;
- honor `eliza.thinking === "off"` in Cerebras mode by mapping it per model: `"none"` for gemma/GLM, `"low"` for gpt-oss; explicit caller `providerOptions.openai.reasoningEffort` still wins.

After the fix (same wire capture): 10/10 probes return content, `finish_reason:"stop"`, `reasoning_tokens: 0`.

topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Add `@elizaos/eliza-hub` as a self-contained workspace package with an Eliza-themed Forgejo deployment, dark/light themes, a local Compose stack, and a portable standalone layout.
- Add Merge Steward: an agent-native merge queue and coordination service with claims, validation budgets, queue simulation, merge trains, Eliza Work/Kanban APIs, OIDC identity, audited overrides, dry-run-first execution, and production evidence gates.
- Add isolated Forgejo Actions runner configuration, Postgres migrations, OpenAPI, backups and restore drills, observability, Terraform/Cloudflare/Hetzner deployment scaffolding, and operator documentation.
- Align the package with elizaOS conventions: `@elizaos/*` names, Node 24 images/runners, monorepo scripts and lockfile, identical `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, MIT metadata, and Poppins OFL attribution.
- Extend the shared coverage gate so subprocess entrypoints require changed tests without falsely treating parent-process LCOV as child-process coverage.

## Why

This gives the team one public folder to inspect, test, extract, and deploy while keeping runtime databases, credentials, runner state, mirrored repositories, Terraform state, backups, and production evidence out of source control. Forgejo remains the Git source of truth; Merge Steward adds agent-scale controls that are not native GitHub or Forgejo concepts.

The package is intentionally honest about readiness: it is a working local demo and production-oriented staging seed, not a GitHub API drop-in or an approved production cutover. Live agent merges remain disabled unless explicit identity, persistence, runner, repository-protection, and private-evidence gates pass.

## Validation

- Node 24 syntax and generated-schema checks: `bun run --cwd packages/eliza-hub check`
- Merge Steward: 796/796 tests passing across 84 suites
- Changed-source coverage gate: 71 in-process source files, 91.52% mean line coverage, 50% required
- Coverage classifier self-test, including 20 explicitly classified subprocess entrypoints
- Real `age` encrypted upload/recovery contract: 5/5 tests passing under Node and Bun

- Prometheus config syntax and 20 alert rules with `promtool`
- Forgejo 15, runner 12, and Node 24 image manifests resolve for amd64/arm64

No cloud account, server, DNS record, remote repository, or running deployment was created or modified. The local Docker daemon was inactive and requires an interactive sudo prompt, so image assembly was not run in this session; a contract test verifies that the runtime image includes its OpenAPI and production-evidence assets.

topPRs.title: feat(chat): liquid-glass ChatOverlay + native transcript renderer (iOS/Android/desktop)
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Overhauls the Milady chat surface across web, iOS, Android, and desktop, and lands a **native chat-transcript renderer** (SwiftUI on iOS, Views on Android, an AppKit spike on macOS) driven by one shared, versioned contract. Renamed `ContinuousChatOverlay → ChatOverlay` throughout.

Three themes:

### 1. Liquid-glass chat surface (real OS material where physics allows)
- The chat sheet floats as liquid glass: a light fill over a heavy `backdrop-filter` (blur + saturate + brightness) so the field behind glows *through* the panel, plus the directional specular rim.
- **Native glass on Capacitor**: the `GlassBridge` plugin (iOS 26 `UIGlassEffect`, Android 12+ Material) was never registered — fixed. The default ember field moves into a **native layer behind a transparent webview** (`setBackdrop`), and the inset sheet anchors a real `UIGlassEffect` panel over it (verified live via lldb: `<UIGlassEffect: …>` + an `EmberBackdropView`/`CAGradientLayer` below the `WKWebView`). The panel's corner radius tracks the sheet's animated corners.
- Maximized chat is a flat neutral `#212121` reading surface (the sheen/gradient read as artifacts full-screen); the exit is a pure cover-layer crossfade (no discrete style swap at the corners); the maximized composer capsule is glassmorphic.
- Desktop: opt-in `NSVisualEffectView` window glass behind the chat-overlay window (`ELIZA_DESKTOP_NATIVE_GLASS=1`).

### 2. Gesture correctness (the pull continuum)
- **maximize → pull-to-half** now settles at a real detent (was: bounced tall / collapsed / stranded a stub). Root causes fixed: an invisible stale grabber captured the restore drag; the restore bookkeeping raced the maximize-release hysteresis; `maximizeFromPull` never settled the height spring (stranded the GPU layer + drag latch); restore releases free-rested instead of completing.
- One **constant pointer-locked drag handle** across pill ↔ input ↔ chat (rendered outside the scale transform, y tracks the panel's visual top).
- Restore drag morphs live (shape springs home, handle fades in under the finger) instead of popping at release.
- Regression e2e: `test:chat-restore-e2e`, `test:chat-restore-continuum-e2e`.

### 3. Native chat-transcript renderer (new)
Everything in the chat renders to **native widgets** — text/markdown, code, choice, follow-ups, form (fields/select/checkbox + validation), workflow, checklist, task card, background swatches, permission card, secret request, tool-call rows, thinking disclosure, failure/retry.

- **One contract** (`eliza.native-transcript/v1`): frames serialized through the *same* `parseSegments` the DOM uses; a typed action envelope back (`message | navigate | prefill | background | retry`). A golden fixture is conformance-tested by every decoder.
- **iOS** SwiftUI, **Android** Views, **macOS** AppKit spike — all one contract.
- Security by construction: secrets are display-only (never transit chat/bridge), permission grant requires a real OS request (no fabrication), navigate/prefill/background stay local intents (never leaked to the agent as chat text).
- Harness demo: `ELIZA_NATIVE_TRANSCRIPT_DEMO=1 bun run --cwd packages/app ios:chat-harness:preview` (full-screen native, DOM composer reserved at the bottom; `eliza:native-transcript-split=1` for side-by-side review).

## Red-team

A 4-lens adversarial red-team (security / iOS correctness / DOM-parity / bridge-lifecycle) + verification judge returned **NO-GO on 5 HIGH findings**; **all fixed** and re-verified:
- iOS scroll no longer yanks a reader who scrolled up (at-bottom guard, DOM/Android parity).
- iOS widget `@State` keyed by stable segment/tool identity, not array offset (locked choice / form draft no longer adopts the wrong view's state).
- Android row fingerprint excludes streaming-volatile fields (widget drafts/locks survive token growth).
- `navigate` routes through the real `dispatchNavigateViewEvent` shape the shell reads.
- Retry is a typed `{kind:retry}` envelope gated to retryable failure kinds (no fabricated chat string).
Plus MEDs: iOS markdown link runs stripped; Android background emits shared preset ids; Android rejects non-v1 schema; Android form no longer trims; harness hides the native list on mid-`show()` unmount; sim-check fails on a native reject.

## Validation

**iOS on-simulator** — all 14 widget types rendered natively and interactive: choice (selection state), form (text input + required validation + submit producing the exact DOM-parity `[form:submit …] {json}`), permission (no grant button), secret (display-only), follow-ups, workflow (step glyphs), tool calls (running/success + duration), thinking, checklist, task, background, code, generated-UI card, failure (gated Retry). Bridge round-trip proven (native tap → `transcriptAction` → script advance → new frame → native re-render).

**Android on-emulator** — native choice + form rendered as native Views (EditText/Spinner/CheckBox/Button); bridge round-trip confirmed in logcat.

**Automated** — 558 UI vitest; native conformance: swiftc -typecheck (0 errors, full module), decode-check, 65-check widget logic script, javac (0), JVM contract 6/6; chat-sheet e2e 296/296; restore e2es green; iOS mirror byte-identical.

## Known follow-ups (non-blocking)
- Native conformance gates (Swift/JVM) are not yet wired into CI (only the TS `spec.test.ts` runs there). Add a macOS Swift lane + JVM lane on fixture/model changes.
- Deep-nesting decode depth cap (hardening; latent, native not production-wired).
- The maximized composer is still CSS glass (an in-page sheet over DOM pixels can't be lensed by an under-webview native panel); a true-native maximized input needs the dual-webview or native-composer architecture.
